utterances.text: [In English] Witness statement of Radomir Gojkovic. Statement summary. Judge Radomir Gojkovic was an investigative judge at the Pec District Court throughout the indictment period. His court has jurisdiction over the Pec, Klina, Istok, Djakovica and Decani municipalities - the Dukagjini area. Lake Radonjic and Rznic were within the area of jurisdiction. In 1998, the court dealt with many cases concerning the KLA, including arms smuggling and the murders of police officers, army soldiers, and civilians. The Dukagjini area became a no-go area for Serb police in mid-1998 because of firearms attacks by the KLA. Police stations were forced to close in the area. On 9th September 1998, the SUP asked Judge Gojkovic to conduct an investigation in relation to the bodies found in the vicinity of Lake Radonjic. He organised a team to attend the scene on the same day in accordance with his responsibilities as investigative judge. They surveyed the area which was secured throughout the investigation by the MUP. It was a very gruesome site with bodies -- with bodies and body parts all over the place. Judge Gojkovic requested the assistance of forensic experts from the Faculty of Forensic Medicine in Belgrade. On 10th September, the team again visited the site and marked and photographed the bodies and body parts. In the afternoon, Judge Gojkovic was told of a possible grave site in Dasinovac and the team went there to investigate. They uncovered bodies and found identification papers on them. On 11 September, the team, under the direction of forensic experts who also attended, began the body recovery operation. Some ten bodies were transported to a temporary mortuary at Hotel Pastrik in Djakovica. The operation continued on the 12th September. On 13 and 14 September, it was not possible to work at the site because of heavy rain. The forensic experts conducted autopsies at the Hotel Pastrik mortuary. On 15th September, body recovery were recommenced at the Lake Radonjic site. The team completed their operation on this day. On 16th September, relatives of missing persons who had been invited to identify the bodies began the identification process. Large numbers simply came to view the remains. The scene was highly emotional and some people were unable to speak. Relatives identified a number of bodies. All of the bodies were placed in metal coffins bearing identification labels. Identified bodies were handed over to their families. The unidentified bodies were taken and buried in the Piskote cemetery in Djakovica. [Interpretation] This is the end of this statement summary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Let me carry on with my questions. First question. Please answer very succinctly. Could you tell us, when it rains in Kosovo, is it heavy rain? Is it like the sort of soft rain you may have in Brittany? What -- is it normal rain? How are rainfalls in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You know why I'm on my feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, how is rain in the Netherlands? Sometimes heavy. Sometimes light. Could you please specify a bit more detail what -- and come to your point. Or is there a general rain pattern in Kosovo? If that's the case, I think we should first ask whether that exists. Please proceed. Perhaps I could ask you: Is rain always the same, Mr. Gojkovic? Do you have one kind of rain or do you have several types of rain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It all depends on the weather conditions. For example, in 1979 there was major flooding and very often there were -- there was bad weather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And sometimes it drizzles as well in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we say that it drizzles or falls softly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre will put further questions to you in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us how it rained in September 1998, when there was this body recovery operation, between the 9th and the 17th of September.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Before the 9th, when we went to the location, it rained a lot. On the 9th, when we got there, we were forced to place an obstacle so that the water would flow out of the channel, which would make the process of finding and pulling the bodies out easier. On the 13th and the 14th, also it rained heavily, and during those two days we didn't do anything in the canal or the canyon towards the Radonjic Lake. In any event, all of this was written in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Secondly, were there stray dogs in Kosovo and in the Dukagjini area throughout the conflict, and notably in August or September 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When we came to the scene on the 9th of September, there were different animals there, cows, horses, and from time to time also dogs appeared, which certainly because of the shooting were frightened and they kept running across from one place to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now see the exhibit the -- that was tendered for MFI purposes by Mr. Di Fazio. That was the video excerpt shown to the previous witness, Exhibit number P1192. And it's now been digitalized.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. If I can just make a correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor said that the identification began on the 16th of September. Probably it's just a technical error. The identification began on the 17th and continued on the 18th and the 19th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it was completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I understand the position, the transcript has now been enhanced and the audio track also enhanced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that we -- okay. Then -- then we have better chances of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My concern is that we should have the interpreters in the interpreters' booths translate what they hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's as usual. Although, perhaps being assisted, checking on what -- what they see is what they hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because sometimes it goes so quickly that interpreting cannot be done immediately, simultaneously. So therefore, as always, the teamwork within the booth, one translating -- one interpreting and the other one following at least whether the transcript reflects what is said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one specification. This video excerpt is part of Exhibit P452, ERN number V006012. I think we can play it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
